message.reasoning_content:
c1 probe: violations confirmed, max_abs_err 0.36 vs tol 0.0025. But wait, c1 had violation_tokens weirdness (only tokens 0 and 64?), but violations=2340 of 6600 — the nonzero indexing was wrong but violations count is decisive. Confirmed.

c2 probe: no violations — errors tiny. Hmm, does that rebut c2? Wait: break at token 32 = chunk 1 first token. _pass_states compares seq[32] (label 1) vs seq[0] (label 0) — differs, so factor zeroed! The claim said compares chunk c's first token to chunk c-1's first token, i.e. seq[32] vs seq[0]... actually the concern was break at chunk c's first token when seq[c*K] and seq[(c-1)*K] are both new label — but seq[(c-1)*K] is chunk c-1's first token; for break at token 32, seq[0]=0, seq[32]=1, differ → zeroed correctly. The leak case would be break at token 32 AND within chunk 0 already having... actually the bug case: break inside chunk 0 (e.g. token 5), then seq[0]=0, seq[32]=1 → factor also zeroed at chunk 1?? Hmm — that would incorrectly zero chunk 1's carry even though the sequence continues! But wait, that leak is different from c2. Anyway, c2 as stated (break exactly at first token of chunk) is actually handled correctly — seq values at chunk starts differ. Actually the c2 statement is wrong: factor IS zeroed. Probe confirms: errors tiny. So c2 is rebutted.

Wait, but the real subtle case for _pass_states: break mid-chunk c-1, e.g. seq changes at token 17. Then seq[16]=0, seq[32]=1 → factor for chunk 1 zeroed — but the state entering chunk 1 should continue from the new sequence started at 17, not be zeroed... but c1's probe shows violations anyway. That's a different failure mode, part of the same mid-chunk break family. Not a separate claim.

Also should I run a probe where the break is mid-chunk and check whether zeroing of factor causes errors even in the final state? c1 probe showed final_max_err 0.24, consistent. Fine.

Finalize both: c1 confirmed, c2 rebutted. No further probes needed. All open claims covered.
